## What We Did

previous cross-validation techniques we have been using are k-folds, here's a new one! k-folds do not account for spatial leakage, geographic cross-validation does. 
    

## Key Concepts

Generalized Linear Modelling, GLM Solution: Link Function 
  Link(g): Map Outcomes -> Predictor's
  without breaking the boundaries rules - there cannot be negative numbers, you cannot go past 1
  Inverse Link(g-1): Map Predictor's -> Outcome 
  turn a mathematical score into real world predictions 
  
Model       Random Component(y)       Bounded Expected Values       Link Function             Inverse Link
Linear      Binomial                  Probability P,(0,1)           Logit Link, ln(P/(1-P))   g^-1, sigmoid function, (e^n/(1+e^n))
Poisson     Poisson                   E(0, infinity)                Log Link, log(u)          e^-1

Probability(p) ; odds: p/(1-p) -> log odds/logit link ; ln(p/1-p) -> B0 + B1....

odds = p/(1-p), how many more times likely is it to happen than it does not? 
if p = 0.8, then the odds are 0.8/(1-0.8) = 4. It is 4 times more likely for something to happen than it does not.
if p = 0.5, then the odds are 0.5/(1-0.5) = 1. There is an even likelihood for something to happen than it does not. 
if p = 0.455, then the odds are 0.455(1-0.455) = 0.835. It is 0.835 more likely for something to happen than it does not. (not very likely)
